title: How Far Does Zero-Shot Go? A Leakage-Aware Evaluation of TimesFM 3 on Post-Release, Multivariate and Controlled Data | Zenodo
note: Zenodo preprint v1.0.0 by one independent researcher, not peer reviewed. Tests TimesFM 3 zero-shot under a protocol frozen before post-release test data were downloaded: real post-release data (load, prices, weather, river flow, FX and interest rates), a Wikipedia memorisation probe, two prospective issues sealed by hash, 7,600 synthetic tasks, and a rerun of Google's fev-bench results.

title: How Far Does Zero-Shot Go? A Leakage-Aware Evaluation of TimesFM 3 on Post-Release, Multivariate and Controlled Data | Zenodo
note: Results: on four structured post-release domains TimesFM 3 has 16% lower MASE and 29% lower scaled quantile loss than a pre-specified classical ensemble (size depends on baseline and weighting); about 5% ahead of Chronos-2. In two overlapping prospective weeks the quantile-loss edge holds, the point-forecast edge on load, prices and river flow does not; 80% intervals cover about 70%.

title: How Far Does Zero-Shot Go? A Leakage-Aware Evaluation of TimesFM 3 on Post-Release, Multivariate and Controlled Data | Zenodo
note: Also: worse than a random walk on exchange rates, interest rates and oil; fails on a saturating synthetic process and after upward level shifts; the Wikipedia probe finds no memorisation effect. Files: PDF and paper sources. Related: dataset DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24194745, code at github.com/alepom/timesfm-zeroshot-study. Weights not redistributed. No citations listed.

title: GitHub - alepom/timesfm-zeroshot-study: How Far Does Zero-Shot Go? A leakage-aware evaluation of TimesFM 3: code, frozen protocol, metrics and seals
note: README results, TimesFM 3 univariate, ratios with 95% CI. Vs classical ensemble on Tier B structured domains: MASE 0.836 (0.786-0.882), SQL 0.707 (0.649-0.764). Prospective load, price, river vs ensemble: MASE 1.073 (0.977-1.175) not resolved, SQL 0.750 (0.648-0.861).

title: GitHub - alepom/timesfm-zeroshot-study: How Far Does Zero-Shot Go? A leakage-aware evaluation of TimesFM 3: code, frozen protocol, metrics and seals

title: timesfm-zeroshot-study/protocol.md at main
note: Protocol v1 dated 28 Oct 2026, frozen by tag; no post-release data downloaded and no model run on test windows before it. Load task: 12 European countries, hourly, horizons 24 and 168 h, origins weekly. Temperature at the capital (ERA5 actuals over the forecast window, an oracle) goes only to the multivariate configurations; the primary contrasts give no model covariates.

title: timesfm-zeroshot-study/protocol.md at main

Weights loaded by Hugging Face revision: google/timesfm-3.0-pytorch, amazon/chronos-2, google/timesfm-2.5-200m-pytorch, NX-AI/TiRex-2. States TimesFM 3 release as 31 Aug 2026.

title: Foundation or Formula? A Simulation-Based Comparison of Google's TimesFM-3 and Classical Time-Series Models
note: From the research call's source list; not fetched. Separate study with pre-registered findings on simulated series, plus M4 and FRED-MD: neither TimesFM 3 nor classical methods dominate; on FRED-MD TimesFM 3 mean MASE 0.607 against AutoARIMA 0.540. No electricity load. The candidate re-implements three of its synthetic processes. Not a replication of the candidate.
